sheet-2.description: Sheet 2, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the railroad station district on the west side of Absecon, between Tenth Street at the top and the vacant ground south of Station Avenue. New Jersey Avenue, also labelled White Horse Pike, runs down the right edge; Ohio Avenue runs parallel to it on the left; the double track of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (P.R.R.) crosses the sheet between them, with a siding curving off near the station. Cedar Avenue joins Ohio Avenue from the west, and Station Avenue crosses the whole sheet, its western end marked not open. Most buildings are frame dwellings with stables and hen houses on deep lots west of the railroad. The commercial buildings stand along the pike: the post office with a drug store, a row of three stores in block construction, a garage with an auto shed, offices, and The Rockingham, a three-and-a-half-storey hotel at the corner of Station Avenue. The Absecon Inn faces Ohio Avenue at the corner of Station Avenue. Beside the tracks stand the Absecon Depot, the grain and feed store of W. B. Etris with scales, a hay shed and a long coal shed, and at the bottom edge a railroad warehouse. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn along the streets with a few hydrants. Block numbers with their older numbers in brackets are printed in the blocks. Adams Avenue is marked leaving New Jersey Avenue in the upper right corner; sheets 4 and 3 adjoin to the north and east.
notes: Adams Avenue is now Mechanic Street.
The modern Absecon Boulevard (US 30) runs through the blocks between the railroad and New Jersey Avenue drawn here; it did not exist in 1923.
The modern railroad line in OpenStreetMap lies about 30 to 40 m west of the tracks as drawn; rail crossings were not used as control.
Cedar Avenue has no modern counterpart in the reference data.
Station Avenue west of Ohio Avenue is marked not open.
The Rockingham hotel, the Absecon Inn and the Absecon Depot of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad are on this sheet.

50 ft. New Jersey Av (White Horse Pike) at right, Ohio Av, Cedar Av, Station Av, Tenth St at top, W.J.&S. R.R. (P.R.R.) through the middle, Absecon Depot, Absecon Inn, The Rockingham, post office. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the centre of Absecon east of New Jersey Avenue (White Horse Pike), which runs down the left edge. Adams Avenue runs diagonally from the pike near Tenth Street down to Church Street, which crosses the sheet from Pitney Road at the top to Shore Road, also called New York Avenue, which runs diagonally across the lower part. South of Shore Road the street continues as S. Church. Station Avenue runs east from the pike and ends at the block above Shore Road. The commercial frontage is along the pike: stores, the 1st National Bank at the corner of Station Avenue, a garage of concrete block for ten cars, offices and storage. On Station Avenue stand a hall over a vacant store, the fire house with a fire bell on a steel tower, a club and a clam storage building. On Church Street are the 1st M.E. Sunday School and the Methodist Meeting House, and a large cemetery fills the ground east of Church Street. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings on large lots, many with automobile sheds. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run along the pike, Church Street and Shore Road. The lower edge is marked vacant beyond and no exposure. Sheets 2 and 4 adjoin to the west and north.
notes: Adams Avenue is now Mechanic Street.
Church north of Shore Road is now West Church Street; S. Church is East Church Street.
Station Avenue now continues east to Shore Road on a different line; that modern junction was excluded.
The junction of Church Street and Shore Road was hand-picked; the detector did not find it.
Methodist Meeting House, 1st M.E. Sunday School, 1st National Bank and the fire house are on this sheet.

50 ft. New Jersey Av (White Horse Pike) at left, Adams Av, Church St, Pitney Road, Station Av, Shore Road or New York Av, S. Church; cemetery, Methodist Meeting House, 1st National Bank, fire house. One part.

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of sheet 4, at 50 ft to an inch, covers the northern part of the village centre: New Jersey Avenue (White Horse Pike) runs down the left of the part, with Centre Street parallel to it further west, and Church Street runs diagonally across the right half. Tenth Street crosses the pike near the bottom and runs north-east to Church Street; Adams Avenue leaves the pike at the bottom edge and Pitney Road leaves Church Street at the lower right. The part is thinly built. Frame dwellings with automobile sheds line the pike and Centre Street; a brick garage with a capacity of twelve cars stands on the pike. The Absecon Presbyterian Church, frame with furnace heat and electric light, stands on the east side of the pike, and the Public School, two storeys of brick with steam heat, stands in the block between Tenth Street and Adams Avenue. A few more dwellings face Church Street. A large unbuilt block (block 4) fills the middle of the part. Water pipes of 4 inches run along the pike and Church Street. The upper edge is marked no exposure. A heavy line cuts off the upper right corner, which is drawn as a separate part showing lots on Ohio Avenue. Sheets 2 and 3 adjoin below.
notes: Tenth Street east of New Jersey Avenue is now School Street; west of it, Southwest Street.
Adams Avenue is now Mechanic Street; Church is West Church Street.
Centre Street has no modern counterpart in the reference data; the modern Absecon Boulevard passes close to its line.
The junction of Church Street and Pitney Road lies just below the sheet edge and was hand-picked from the drawn street edges.
Public School and Absecon Presbyterian Church are on this part.

50 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy line: main part New Jersey Av (White Horse Pike), Centre, Tenth, Church, Pitney Road, Adams Av, public school, Presbyterian church; part 2 at upper right a strip along Ohio Av (continues sheet 2 to the north) with its own north arrow.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: upper right corner: lots on Ohio Avenue north of sheet 2 (no street junction; only Ohio Avenue is drawn; needs step 6b: lot lines matched to the top of sheet 2, or a modern cross street (Showellton Avenue) confirmed on the sheet).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5, at 50 ft to an inch, covers a residential area on the north-east side of Absecon around the fork where Faunce's Landing Road leaves Shore Road. Shore Road, also labelled New York Avenue, crosses the top of the sheet and continues diagonally towards the lower right as New York Avenue; Faunce's Landing Road runs down from the fork across the sheet to the bottom edge, and the road continues north from the fork beyond the top edge. Natalie Terrace runs parallel to Faunce's Landing Road on the left and stops short of the bottom. A street marked Drive, drawn with dashed lines as not yet open, leaves Faunce's Landing Road near the bottom. The sheet is sparsely built: about twenty frame dwellings, most with automobile sheds, on large lots along Shore Road, Natalie Terrace and Faunce's Landing Road, two of them of concrete block. Much of the area is unbuilt, with large block numbers (19 to 23) in open ground, and the top and bottom edges are marked no exposure and vacant beyond. A 4 inch water pipe runs along Shore Road and New York Avenue. The sheet is turned on the page: north points to the upper right.
notes: Faunce's Landing Road is now East Faunce Landing Road; its continuation north of the fork is West Faunce Landing Road.
The sheet is turned: north points to the upper right (about 66 degrees).
Only two junctions survive on this sheet, so it is placed by a two-point helmert transformation.
The dashed Drive near the bottom was not open in 1923 and has no modern counterpart here.
50 ft. Shore Road or New York Av, Natalie Terrace, Faunce's Landing Road, a dashed Drive (not open). One part, sparse.

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of sheet 6, at 100 ft to an inch, covers the south end of Absecon along Shore Road, also labelled New York Avenue, which runs straight down the sheet from above Iowa Avenue to the Pleasantville city line and beyond. West of Shore Road the cross streets are Iowa Avenue, Bolton Avenue, W. Nevada Avenue, Oregon Avenue and California Avenue, with long narrow lots and large unbuilt blocks between them. East of Shore Road a grid is laid out: Bolton, Lee and Colorado Avenues cross Eighth Avenue, The Boulevard, Seventh Avenue and Ocean Avenue, and Nevada Avenue along the bottom of the grid carries the dash-dot City Line. Below it the blocks are lettered City of Pleasantville and left blank, apart from California Avenue at the bottom edge. The area is a suburb of frame dwellings, many with automobile sheds and coops; long poultry houses and a water tank on a steel tower stand in block 33 east of Shore Road above Bolton Avenue. Most blocks east of The Boulevard are laid out in lots but empty. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn along Shore Road, Iowa and Nevada Avenues with hydrants. A heavy line cuts off the upper right corner, which shows Shore Road at East Illinois Avenue as a separate part. The scale note reads Scale 100 ft to an inch.
notes: Shore Road is now South Shore Road, and North Main Street south of Nevada Avenue in Pleasantville.
The Boulevard is now Franklin Boulevard (North Franklin Boulevard south of Nevada Avenue).
Eighth Avenue is now 8th Street; Seventh Avenue is 7th Avenue; Lee Avenue east of Shore Road is East Lee Avenue.
Colorado Avenue is drawn ending short of The Boulevard; the modern East Colorado Avenue is on a different line and was not used.
Nevada Avenue is drawn about 32 to 39 ft wide against about 60 to 70 ft today; its junctions carry 3 to 5 m residuals.
The Absecon and Pleasantville city line follows Nevada Avenue.

100 ft (Scale 100 ft to an inch). Two parts separated by a heavy line: main part Shore Road or New York Av, Iowa, Bolton, Lee, Colorado, W. sheet-6-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 6, at 100 ft to an inch, is the upper right corner of the sheet, cut off by a heavy line. It shows Shore Road running down the part from above East Illinois Avenue to Iowa Avenue, which is drawn with dashed lines at the bottom of the part. E. Illinois Avenue leaves Shore Road eastward and curves across the top of the part to the tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (P.R.R.), which cross the upper right corner. The part is lightly built: frame dwellings with automobile sheds and coops on both sides of Shore Road and along E. Illinois Avenue, one dwelling of tile, an ice house, storage buildings and a long coop. Block numbers 31 and 33 continue those of the main part. A 6 inch water pipe runs along Shore Road with hydrants. The part carries its own north arrow, pointing to the upper left as on the main part, and the sheet cartouche with the note Scale 100 ft to an inch.
notes: E. Illinois Avenue is now East Illinois Avenue; Shore Road is South Shore Road.
